blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Partial shape matching is a crucial yet underexplored problem in 3D vision, with significant relevance to real-world scenarios where shapes are often only partially observed. Existing feature descriptors face difficulties in this setting, as traditional representations either struggle with the boundaries of partial shapes or heavily depend on the shape's spatial position. While existing approaches have employed DINO features for partial shape matching, these features are not inherently suited for handling partial observations. In this work, we propose a method to refine DINO features using LoRA-based self-supervised learning, enabling the generation of feature descriptors that are robust to partiality. Our features substantially improve performance on partial shape matching compared to traditional or vision foundation features. Additionally, when integrated into existing partial shape matching pipelines, we achieve state-of-the-art results on partial shape matching and left-right prediction benchmarks.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Finding dense correspondences between 3D deformable shapes is a fundamental step in understanding geometric data, enabling several downstream tasks, including information transfer and learning statistical models.
Specifically, when the geometries do not share the same identity (e.g., different humans) and undergo non‑rigid deformations (e.g., different poses), establishing such correspondences remains an open research problem.
The challenge is further exacerbated when one (or both) of the shapes comes from partial observations, a common real-world case due to occlusions, acquisition noise, or local errors in the 3D reconstruction.
blocks.zh:
在3D可变形形状之间找到密集的对应,是理解几何数据的根本步骤,能够完成几个下游任务,包括信息传输和学习统计模型.
具体地说,当地缘变相体不具有相同特征(例如不同的人类)并经历非"硬"变形(例如不同的外形)时,建立这种函证仍然是一个开放的研究问题.
当一个(或两个)外形来自部分观察,一个常见的现实世界案例由3D重建中被占据,获得噪音或局部出错而导致时,这一挑战会更趋严重.

blocks.en:
Scholars have relied on handcrafted descriptors [ 55 , 5 , 57 ] for decades, both standalone and as input to deep learning pipelines.
Such descriptors demonstrate powerful capabilities for full shapes, but they often rely on theoretical premises (e.g., watertight meshes with the same topology) that make them impractical for partial use cases.
Recently, the emergence of foundation models like DINO [ 14 , 44 , 53 ] or Stable Diffusion [ 50 ] has introduced a new class of features.
Trained on billions of images in a self-supervised manner, these models demonstrate an impressive ability to characterise points semantically, while being robust across deformations and identities.
Such features have been applied to various computer vision tasks, including detection [ 40 , 63 ] , segmentation [ 36 , 60 ] , and, more recently, 3D shape matching [ 19 ] .
However, these models have a limited understanding of 3D geometry, often exhibiting geometrical confusion, such as left-right mismatches and occlusions/disocclusions.
These problems persist even in the most advanced foundation models (DINOv3 [ 53 ] ), as we will demonstrate in our experiments.
While recent works have explored 2D-based fine-tuning strategies [ 30 ] , models trained solely on single-view images lack true 3D grounding.
Achieving this physical understanding requires incorporating 3D information directly into the training process.
blocks.zh:
学者几十年来一直依赖手工描述 [55, 5, 57] , 两者都是独立的,并作为深层学习管道的投入.
这种描述符表现出了全形的强大能力,但是它们常常依赖于理论前提(例如具有同一种地貌的紧水相间),使得它们对于部分使用的案例不切实际.
最近,DINO [14,44,53] 或稳定分化 [50]等基础模型的出现,引入了一个新的特征类别.
这些模型以自我监督的方式对数十亿个图像进行训练,显示出令人印象深刻的能力,既能对成形点和身份点进行定性,又能强健地跨越变形和身份点.
这些特性被应用到各种计算机视觉任务中,包括检测[40,63],分化[36,60],以及最近匹配[19]的3D形状.
然而,这些模型对3D几何学的理解有限,往往表现出几何上的混乱,如左相右相克和被隔离/被隔离.
即使在最先进的基础模型(DINOv3[53])中,这些问题仍然存在,我们将在我们的实验中证明这一点。
虽然近期的作品探索了基于2D的微调策略[30],但仅接受单景图像培训的模型缺乏真正的3D地基.
要实现这种实际理解,就必须将三维信息直接纳入培训过程。

blocks.en:
While training a new foundation model for 3D shapes from scratch would require a huge amount of data and resources, we propose a more natural and elegant solution that injects 3D awareness into 2D foundation features.
We propose GeoLoRA (Geometry-Aware Low-Rank Adaptation) , a new self-supervised approach that, using only synthetic data, informs the backbone 2D foundation features of the 3D structure.
Our idea is to start from full shapes and generate synthetic partial versions of them, using procedures to simulate real occlusions or artefacts.
Since the partial shapes originate from the full ones, they also enjoy a natural 3D correspondence.
We use this information to supervise a lightweight LoRA [ 33 ] module on top of the 2D foundation model, rendering multiple images for both the full and partial shapes, and optimising the features to be aligned between the two.
Finally, unlike fully 2D approaches, since we have access to the 3D geometry of the shapes that generated the image, we incorporate a geodesic penalty into our contrastive loss, providing a strong geometric cue.
In practice, we learn a feature space where dissimilar points are pushed away proportionally to their distance on the object surface.
blocks.zh:
虽然从零开始培训3D形状的新的基础模型需要大量的数据和资源,但我们提出一个更自然和优雅的解决方案,将3D意识注入2D的基础特征.
我们提出GeoLORA(Geometry-Aware Low-Rank adaption),这是一种新的自我监督的方法,它只使用合成数据,告知了3D结构的骨干2D基础特征.
我们的想法是,从完整的外形开始,并产生合成的部分版本,利用程序来模拟真正的隐形物或手工艺品.

blocks.en:
As a result, we achieve the best features for partial-to-full shape matching available to date.
We surpass handcrafted and 2D foundation feature alternatives across different partiality classes and datasets, both in partial-to-full and partial-to-partial settings (some results are shown in Fig. 1 ).
The refined features integrate seamlessly with state-of-the-art matching methods, boosting their performance.
They also show better chirality (left-right disambiguation) than the original backbone features, suggesting that partial-to-full matching can be a useful auxiliary task for enhancing the geometrical understanding of foundation models.
In summary, our contributions are: • We propose GeoLoRA , a novel framework to inject 3D information into 2D foundation features for 3D partial observations. • We demonstrate that GeoLoRA produces the best features for partial 3D shapes across multiple benchmark datasets. • We show that these features improve SOTA performance in downstream tasks as partial-to-full and partial-to-partial shape matching , and strengthen the model’s ability to handle geometrical challenges (e.g., left-right disambiguation).
blocks.zh:
因此,我们实现了迄今为止局部到完全形状匹配的最佳特征.
我们超越了手工制作和2D基础,在部分到完全和部分到部分的环境下,不同部分类别和数据集都有替代品(一些结果见图1)。
精细的特征与最先进的相配方法无缝地融合,提升了它们的性能.
它们也表现出了比原始主干特征更好的奇特性(左-右相分化),表明部分到完全匹配可以是一个有用的辅助任务来增强对地基模型的几何理解.
简而言之,我们的贡献是:我们提议GeoLora,这是一个将3D信息注入3D部分观测的2D基础功能的新框架。 我们证明,GeoLORA为多个基准数据集的部分三维外形提供了最佳特征。 我们显示,这些特征提高了SOTA在下游任务中的性能,作为部分到完全和部分到部分形状的匹配,并加强了模型处理几何挑战的能力(如左向分解等).

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: In this section, we give an overview of the most relevant works, including partial shape matching, features for shape matching and self-supervised learning approaches.
blocks.zh: 在本节中,我们概述了最相关的作品,包括部分外形相配,外形相配的特征和自我监督的学习方法.

blocks.en: 2.1 Partial Shape Matching
blocks.zh: 2.1 部分形状匹配

blocks.en: While many full-to-full shape matching works use spatial features [ 28 , 25 , 56 , 13 ] or functional maps [ 45 , 38 , 29 , 12 , 6 ] , the task of matching partial observations remains a challenging open problem [ 23 ] . We focus on the most important partial-shape matching works in this section and refer to these surveys [ 51 , 17 ] for an in-depth overview of general shape matching methods.
blocks.zh: 虽然许多全到全相外形相配的作品使用空间特征[28,25,56,13]或功能地图[45,38,29,12,6],但部分观测相配的任务仍然是一个挑战性的开放问题[23]. 我们注重本节中最重要的部分形状相配的作品,并参考这些调查[51,17],以深入地概括一般形状相配方法.

blocks.en:
In partial-to-full shape matching, we aim to find correspondences between a partial observation and a full template shape.
PFM [ 48 ] analyses partial shape matching with functional maps and uses the slanted diagonal structure for optimisation.
DPFM [ 3 ] incorporates this idea into a deep learning framework and adds a cross-attention refinement module for feature communication between the partial and full shape.
ULRSSM [ 12 ] ensures that the obtained functional map is coupled with valid point-wise correspondences.
Other partial shape matching methods focus on distance preservation [ 8 , 9 ] for isometric matching.
Axiomatic methods [ 22 , 49 , 26 ] ensure smoothness through geometric consistency with an (Integer) Linear Programs.
blocks.zh:
在部分到完整的外形匹配中,我们的目标是找到部分观察和完整的模板外形之间的对应.
PFM [48] 分析部分外形与功能地图相匹配,并使用斜向对角结构来优化.
DPFM[3]将这一想法纳入深层学习框架,并增加了一个跨心修饰模块,用于部分外形和全外形之间的特征交流.
ULRSSM [12] 确保获得的功能映射与有效的出点对应相配合.
其他部分外形相配方法侧重于同位素相配的距离保存[8,9].
定理方法[22,49,26]通过几何上与一(整)行程序的一致性,确保平滑.

blocks.en:
Partial-to-partial shape matching is even more challenging, as both shapes have missing parts that may also differ between the two.
In this setting, we not only want to find correspondences between shapes, but also determine the regions that overlap.
DPFM [ 3 ] presents a supervised method, which predicts both overlap regions and correspondences.
Echo-Match [ 62 ] improves DPFM’s overlap predictor and shows the usefulness of 2D image foundation features for partial-to-partial shape matching.
Besides learning-based frameworks, GC-PPSM [ 21 ] and Partial-GeCo [ 24 ] tackle the problem using a (non-)linear integer program, while enforcing geometric consistency.
blocks.zh:
部分到部分的外形相配更具有挑战性,因为两种外形都有缺失的部分,它们之间也可能有所不同.
在此背景下,我们不仅想找到形状之间的对应,而且还想确定重叠的区域.
DPFM[3]提出了一种被监督的方法,它预测了重叠的区域和函证.
Echo-Match [62] 改进了DPFM的重叠预测器,并显示了2D图像基础特性对部分到部分形状匹配的实用性.
除了以学习为基础的框架外,GC-PPSM[21]和Pacific-GeCo[24]还使用(非)线性整数程序解决问题,同时执行几何一致性。

blocks.en: 2.2 Features for Shape Matching
blocks.zh: 2.2 形状匹配的特点

blocks.en:
Most full-to-full shape matching methods start from hand-crafted geometrical features, such as the Heat Kernel Signature [ 55 ] and the Wave Kernel Signature [ 5 ] .
While showing success in full-to-full shape matching, partial shape matching features are fragile due to missing parts and boundaries. Hence, SHOT [ 57 ] features, or the vertex coordinates themselves, are generally preferred as input. On the other hand, their extrinsic nature leads to biases toward shape alignment, as shown in [ 23 , 62 , 4 ] .
blocks.zh:
大多数全到全相外形相配的方法都从手工制作的几何特征开始,例如热克内尔签名[55]和波克内尔签名[5].
虽然在全到全外形匹配中显示成功,但部分外形匹配特征由于缺少零件和边界而变得脆弱. 因此,SHOT[57]特征或顶点坐标本身通常被选作输入. 另一方面,如[23、62、4]所示,它们的外在性质导致偏差,导致形状对齐。

blocks.en:
Vision foundation models (VFM), such as the DINO family [ 14 , 44 , 53 ] , masked autoencoders [ 31 ] , and Segment Anything [ 35 ] are trained on a large corpus of data providing general-purpose features for various tasks.
They also have proven useful in numerous domains outside of natural image analysis.
Examples include adaptations in medicine for multi-modal images [ 52 ] , registration [ 54 ] , and volume classification [ 43 ] , as well as in robotics [ 40 , 18 , 66 , 59 ] .
The field of shape matching has also leveraged these general-purpose features in seminal works on full [ 19 , 39 , 58 ] and partial [ 62 ] shape matching.
Our work distinguishes itself from prior shape analysis papers by being the first to not only utilise the features generated by DINOv3 as input, but also incorporates 3D information about partial shapes into the foundation model.
However, it is worth mentioning that 2D foundation models suffer from geometrical ambiguity [ 27 , 64 ] .
Several works rely on 2D tasks, incorporating geometrical augmentations such as image flipping [ 65 ] , or optimal transport objectives to account for (dis-)occlusions in the images [ 30 ] .
Involving 3D data has been significantly less explored, and generally limited to textured rigid objects [ 46 ] .
To the best of our knowledge, we are the first to inject geometry awareness into foundation models for partial, non-rigid, untextured 3D shape matching.
blocks.zh:
远景基础模型(VFM),如DINO家族[14,44,53],蒙面自编码器[31],和September Anything [35]都接受了大量数据的培训,为各种任务提供通用特征.
事实证明,它们在自然图像分析以外的许多领域也是有用的。
实例包括医学对多模式图像的修改[52]、注册[54]、量分类[43]以及机器人[40、18、66、59]。
外形相配领域也利用了这些通用地物在开创性作品中的全部[19,39,58]和部分[62]外形相配.
我们的工作与先前的形状分析文件有区别,它首先不仅利用DINOv3产生的特性作为投入,而且还将关于部分形状的三维信息纳入基础模型。
然而,值得一提的是,2D基础模型存在几何模糊性[27,64].
一些作品依赖于2D任务,包含几何增强,如图像翻转[65],或优化的传输目标,以说明图像中的(去)分量[30].
涉及立体数据的研究少得多,一般限于有纹理的刚性物体[46]。
就我们所知,我们首先将几何意识注入基础模型中,进行局部的,非刚性,无纹的3D外形相配.

blocks.en: 2.3 Self-Supervised Learning for 3D Shapes
blocks.zh: 2.3 3D形状的自我监督学习

blocks.en:
PointContrast [ 61 ] introduces the contrastive loss called PointInfoNCE for pre-training on 3D point clouds, aiming to facilitate transfer learning to high-level scene understanding.
This approach was later extended by follow-up works [ 15 , 32 ] , all of which tackle static scenes, whereas we focus on non-rigid, deformed shapes.
In [ 4 ] , the authors show that pre-training on rigid scenes can improve non-rigid shape matching performance by optimising the receptive field size of local features.
In [ 11 ] , they use a self-supervised learning approach together with the functional map framework to improve matching performance for shapes represented as point clouds.
While these methods show the effectiveness of self-supervised learning for 3D shapes, they do not yet tackle partial non-rigid shapes at a large scale using vision foundation models.
blocks.zh:
PointContrast [61] 引入了名为PointInfonCE的对比性损失,用于3D点云的预训,旨在为将学习转移到高水平的场景理解提供方便.
这种方法后来被后续作品[15,32]所推广,这些作品都解决了静态场景,而我们则专注于非刚性,畸形的外形.
在[4]中,作者们表明,对僵硬场景的预训可以通过优化当地地物的可接受性场积来提高非刚性形状相配性能.
在 [11] 中,他们使用自我监督的学习方法与功能图框架一起来改进以点云为代表的形状的匹配性能.
虽然这些方法显示了自控学习对3D形状的有效性,但是它们还没有使用视觉基础模型大规模地解决部分非刚性形状.

blocks.en: 3 Method
blocks.zh: 3 方法

blocks.en:
Figure 2 : Our Self-Supervised Training Pipeline: Given a full mesh 𝒳 \mathcal{X} ,
we first generate a partial observation 𝒴 \mathcal{Y} .
After randomly rotating both shapes with different rotation matrices around the Y-axis, we render the partial and full shape from different perspectives with cameras 𝒞 \mathcal{C} .
For every camera c i ∈ 𝒞 c^{i}\in\mathcal{C} , we obtain an image 𝐈 𝒳 i \mathbf{I}^{i}_{\mathcal{X}} of the full shape, which is then passed through a frozen DINOv3 architecture with a LoRA module with rank r r to extract pixel-wise features 𝐐 𝒳 i \mathbf{Q}^{i}_{\mathcal{X}} .
These are then backprojected on the shape and averaged to get vertex-wise features 𝐅 𝒳 \mathbf{F}_{\mathcal{X}} .
Similarly, we proceed for the partial shape 𝒴 \mathcal{Y} .
Finally, we use the Geodesic-Aware PointInfoNCE contrastive loss to align corresponding vertices of both shapes and separate all others based on geodesic distance.
In our experiments we use 4 4 views for the partial and 9 9 views for the full shape.

blocks.en:
GeoLoRA is the first self-supervised approach that develops geometry-aware foundation features for partial shape matching.
We start by generating partial shapes from full ones, mimicking synthetic occlusions and missing surfaces.
Then, we use these pairs of full and partial shapes, and train a LoRA module to align the features between them, via a novel geodesic-based contrastive loss.
Figure 2 illustrates our approach, with individual components detailed below.
For better understandability, we refer to the supplementary material for a comprehensive outline of our notation.
blocks.zh:
GeoLora是第一个开发出几何感知地基特征进行部分外形匹配的自控方法.
我们首先从完整的形状中产生部分形状,模仿合成的封入和缺失的表面.

blocks.en:
After the partial shape generation, we collect the foundation features for the full shape 𝒳 \mathcal{X} and its partial counterpart 𝒴 \mathcal{Y} .
We randomly rotate the shapes around the Y-axis, and following Diff3f [ 19 ] sample N N different cameras around the full shape 𝒳 \mathcal{X} , to obtain a set of cameras 𝒞 = ( c 1 , … , c N ) \mathcal{C}=(c^{1},...,c^{N}) .
For each camera c i c^{i} , we render an image 𝐈 𝒳 i ∈ ℝ 512 × 512 × 3 \mathbf{I}^{i}_{\mathcal{X}}\in\mathbb{R}^{512\times 512\times 3} from its viewpoint.
Each image is then processed by a DINOv3 [ 53 ] module.
Our goal is to improve the features obtained from the foundation model.
However, fine-tuning the entire foundation model would cause an additional computational burden.
Hence, we keep the DINOv3 backbone frozen during training and add a low-rank adaptation (LoRA) module with rank r r on top [ 33 ] .
We use LoRA in a siamese fashion, meaning that the weights are shared between the full and partial observations.
For every image 𝐈 𝒳 i \mathbf{I}^{i}_{\mathcal{X}} we obtain pixel-wise features 𝐐 𝒳 i ∈ ℝ 512 × 512 × 768 \mathbf{Q}^{i}_{\mathcal{X}}\in\mathbb{R}^{512\times 512\times 768} , which we backproject to the mesh by averaging all pixels of all images observing a given vertex.
This produces vertex-wise features for the full shape, 𝐅 𝒳 ∈ ℝ | 𝐕 𝒳 | × 768 \mathbf{F}_{\mathcal{X}}\in\mathbb{R}^{|\mathbf{V}_{\mathcal{X}}|\times 768} .
We apply the same procedure to the partial shape 𝒴 \mathcal{Y} by sampling N N cameras around it, resulting in a set of cameras 𝒞 \mathcal{C} . For each camera c i ∈ 𝒞 c_{i}\in\mathcal{C} , we extract image features 𝐐 𝒴 i \mathbf{Q}^{i}_{\mathcal{Y}} , which we then backproject to produce vertex-wise features 𝐅 𝒴 ∈ ℝ | 𝐕 𝒴 | × 768 \mathbf{F}_{\mathcal{Y}}\in\mathbb{R}^{|\mathbf{V}_{\mathcal{Y}}|\times 768} .
At this point, it is worth highlighting that the full and partial shapes represent the same object in the same pose.
At first glance, this may appear restrictive, as we actually aim to solve for non-rigid shape matching, and at inference time, we can expect to match objects that have undergone various deformations.
However, we believe our training setting exactly represents the task our backbone should solve: recover the semantics of an observed partial shape, as if it belonged to a full geometry.
In practice, we set a small number of N = 9 N=9 cameras for the full shape and N = 4 N=4 for its partial observation ensuring efficient model training.

blocks.en:
We demonstrate the effectiveness of GeoLoRA with an extensive set of experiments. First, we compare the matching induced by the features from GeoLoRA with those obtained from handcrafted and learning-based alternatives.
Further, we incorporate GeoLoRA features into partial-to-full and partial-to-partial shape matching SOTA methods, demonstrating their natural blend with them.
To show the improved geometrical representation, we also test their left-right characterisation on partial shapes.
Finally, we justify our design choices through an ablation study.

我们通过一系列广泛的实验来证明地球海洋管理局的有效性。 首先,我们比较了GeoLora的特征所引发的匹配与手工和以学习为基础的替代方法获得的匹配。
此外,我们将GeoLORA特征纳入部分到完全和部分到部分的形状,与SOTA方法相匹配,显示了它们与它们的自然混合.
为了显示改善的几何性能,我们还用部分形状测试他们的左-右特征.
最后,我们通过一项消化研究来证明我们的设计选择是合理的。

blocks.en: 4.1 Implementation Details
blocks.zh: 4.1 详细执行情况

blocks.en:
We use the DINOv3 ViT-B/16 backbone and integrate LoRA modules into all attention layers.
The LoRA configuration uses a rank of r = 16 r=16 and a scaling factor of α = 32 \alpha=32 .
To maintain training feasibility, we use 9 9 views for each full shape and 4 4 views for each partial shape. During inference, we increase the number of views to 49 49 .
In each training batch, we generate two partial observations per full shape.
All methods are trained for 50.000 50.000 iterations.

LORA配置使用r=16 r=16的分级和α=32\alpha=32的缩放系数.
为了保持训练的可行性,我们使用9个观点,每个完整的形状,4个观点,每个部分形状。 在推论期间,我们把意见数目增加到49 49。
在每批训练中,我们每个整形产生两个部分的观测.
所有方法都经过培训,可进行50 000 50 000次重复。

blocks.en: 4.2 Datasets
blocks.zh: 4.2 数据集

blocks.en:
For partial-to-full matching, we use the Shrec16 dataset [ 16 ] , which is based on the synthetic shapes of Tosca [ 10 ] . It contains 76 76 nearly-isometric shapes from eight different classes of humans and animals. Each class has one template mesh in a neutral pose.
The partial shapes are divided into Cuts and Holes .
The Cuts dataset contains partial shapes cut by a plane, whereas the Holes dataset contains shapes with irregular holes that are produced by an erosion process. We rely on the Cuts24 split [ 21 ] to ensure that no shapes from the test set have been used for training. We also test on the Pfaust dataset [ 8 ] , a modification of [ 7 ] , where 10 10 different humans ( 8 8 are used for training and 2 2 for testing) are seen in 10 10 different poses. Pfaust processes the dataset adding artificial holes of varying difficulty, including Pfaust-M (medium difficulty) and Pfaust-H (hard difficulty). A relevant dataset is also CP2P24 [ 3 , 21 ] , a partial-to-partial matching dataset based on Shrec16 , including cuts for near-isometric shapes. We also stress-test our method on non-isometric partial correspondence tasks using the Psmal dataset [ 21 ] , derived from Smal [ 67 ] by adding artificial cuts. For Psmal , the train and test sets are split by different animal species. Finally, we also include the recent BeCoS dataset [ 23 ] , which integrates both humanoid and animal shapes from Faust [ 7 ] , Scape [ 2 ] , Smal [ 67 ] , DT4D [ 37 ] , Tosca [ 10 ] , Kids [ 47 ] , and Shrec20 [ 20 ] , totaling over 2,500 unique shapes. BeCoS provides the most extensive benchmark, with full-to-full, partial-to-full, and partial-to-partial shape instances.

blocks.en: 4.3 Metrics
blocks.zh: 4.3 计量

blocks.en:
We report the widely used Geodesic Error metric following the Princeton Protocol [ 34 ] .
The error is scaled by the shape diameter of the corresponding full shape, also for partial-to-partial shape matching [ 21 ] .
We report the mean geodesic error over all vertices in the dataset.
For the partial-to-partial datasets, we report the geodesic error on the overlapping region.
As proposed in [ 21 ] , we use the Intersection over Union (IoU) to evaluate the overlap region prediction.
For a shape 𝒴 \mathcal{Y} we compare the overlap prediction P 𝒴 ∈ { 0 , 1 } | 𝐕 𝒴 | P_{\mathcal{Y}}\in\{0,1\}^{|\mathbf{V}_{\mathcal{Y}}|} and the ground truth overlap G 𝒴 ∈ { 0 , 1 } | 𝐕 𝒴 | G_{\mathcal{Y}}\in\{0,1\}^{|\mathbf{V}_{\mathcal{Y}}|} , which includes for every vertex in 𝐕 𝒴 \mathbf{V}_{\mathcal{Y}} if it is in the overlapping region.

Baselines and Data. We compare matchings induced by GeoLoRA with established handcrafted descriptors—WKS [ 5 ] and HKS [ 55 ] —as well as features from foundation models DINOv2 [ 44 ] , DINOv3 [ 44 ] , and Diff3f [ 19 ] .
For DINOv2, DINOv3, and GeoLoRA, we utilise 49 views, providing the optimal balance between performance and runtime (see our ablation study).
For training our self-supervised network, we always use the full shapes from the training set, ensuring that no shapes of the test/validation set have been seen during training.
Since Shrec16 ’s training set includes full shapes of partials used in its test set, we create BeCoS *, the BeCoS training dataset excluding Shrec16 data.
We evaluate the geodesic error of these feature extractors by performing a nearest-neighbour search using the L2 distance.

为了训练我们自我监督的网络,我们总是使用训练集的全外形,确保训练期间没有看到测试/验证集的外形.
由于Shrec16的训练集包含了测试集中使用的部分的全外形,我们创建了BeCoS *,BeCoS训练数据集不包括了Shrec16的数据.
我们通过使用L2距离进行近邻搜索来评估这些地貌提取器的大地测量误差.

blocks.en: Results We report the quantiative analysis in Table 1 . We observe a significant improvement in terms of geodesic error over all the datasets, particularly for the very challenging BeCoS dataset. We report qualitative examples in Figure 3 . Our improvement is noticeable across all datasets, with better left-right disambiguation compared to using DINOv3 features directly.

blocks.zh: 4.5 与匹配方法相结合

blocks.en: State-of-the-art shape matching methods do not use features as they are, but further refine them for specific datasets and settings. Hence, we also explore the applicability of our features as replacements for alternatives in matching pipelines, both for the partial-to-full and partial-to-partial matching methods. Notice that this latter is a case for which we have not explicitly trained our features, and hence will test their generality.
blocks.zh: 最先进的外形匹配方法并不使用原样的特征,而是为特定数据集和设置而进一步完善. 因此,我们还探索了我们作为替代物在配对管道中的应用性,无论是部分配对还是部分配对方法。 请注意,后者是一个我们没有明确培训我们特征的案例,因此将检验其普遍性。

blocks.en:
Partial-to-Full Shape Matching For partial-to-full shape matching, we use SOTA unsupervised methods, DPFM [ 3 ] and ULRSSM [ 12 ] .
While originally they used spatial coordinates as input, this has been shown to heavily depend on the alignment of shapes in the datasets [ 23 , 62 , 4 ] .
Therefore, we use vision foundation features as input.
We compare GeoLoRA with DINOv3 [ 53 ] features, as this latter is the second-best-performing (see Sec. 4.4 ).
We report quantitative results for the partial-to-full matching in Table 2 , where the numbers in brackets show the features after test-time adaptation from ULRSSM.
We show a qualitative example in Figure 4 .

For both methods, we observe the improvement provided by GeoLoRA over the DINOv3 alternative.
Note that for the BeCoS dataset, the geodesic error is higher than when using GeoLoRA directly.
We see two reasons for this: Firstly, BeCoS is the only dataset providing unnormalised shapes, meaning that the size ratio of the shapes is realistic (e.g., an elephant is larger than a mouse).

Partial-to-Partial Shape Matching Since no unsupervised methods are available for partial-to-partial shape matching, we rely on two SOTA supervised methods DPFM [ 3 ] and EchoMatch [ 62 ] .
In this setting, in conjunction with the correspondence, we also aim to identify the points that have a correspondence between the shapes, and thus determine their overlapping regions.
Following [ 21 ] , we report both the geodesic error and the IoU in Table 3 .
For BeCoS and Psmal , we see improvement in terms of correspondence quality and overlap prediction.
For the CP2P24 dataset, we observe similar results with GeoLoRA compared to DINOv3, likely because the supervision prevents it from benefiting from improved feature descriptors.

blocks.zh: 4.7 申请

blocks.en:
Distinguishing the left and right of a mesh is an essential task for 3D shape analysis.
We train the network from [ 58 ] with different features: DINOv3, GeoLoRA, and features obtained by our pipeline, but with the PointInfoNCE loss.
For training, we use the BeCoS full-to-full train set, and we evaluate on the partial shapes from the BeCoS partial-to-full test set. From the results in Table 6 , we observe that GeoLoRA provides significant improvement in terms of accuracy. The qualitative improvement can be seen in Figure 5 , even for highly partial shapes.
In comparison to the PointInfoNCE loss, our formulation further improves the left-right prediction.

blocks.en:
Mapping a partial observation to a full template is particularly relevant for real-world applications, such as interpreting data from acquisition pipelines.
In Figure 6 , we report an illustrative result, obtained from a depth-sensor-based body scanner.
During the acquisition, the user was partially misaligned with respect to the capturing volume.
While DINOv3 fails to recover the semantics of such ruined geometry, our features show robustness. We found this result really exciting, as it can open up new techniques for non-rigid reconstruction of moving objects.

blocks.en: 5 Discussion and Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5. 讨论和结论

blocks.en:
We introduced GeoLoRA, a novel self-supervised approach for learning robust features on partial 3D shapes. By relying solely on synthetic data and self-supervised tasks, we demonstrated that our features not only possess a better geometrical understanding than 2D foundation backbones but are also the best available features to date for partial-to-partial and partial-to-full shape matching.
The main limitation is likely inherited from DINOv3, which involves pretraining on natural images and thus incorporates a bias toward shapes in an upright orientation.
Although 3D objects are often assumed to be upright, this assumption might worsen the results in upside-down poses.
While our method still outperforms the DINOv3 baseline on upside-down poses, as shown in the supplementary material, both approaches show reduced performance compared to their results on upright-oriented shapes.
Overall, our work demonstrates that adapting vision foundation models through low-rank adaptation can substantially advance partial shape understanding.
In the future, our work could be extended to also consider external clutter and man-made objects.
Ultimately, we view our work as a promising step toward bridging the gap between large-scale image representations and 3D geometry, providing valuable insights to the broader communities of shape analysis and 3D vision.
blocks.zh:
我们介绍了GeoLORA, 这是一种新的自我监督的方法, 用来学习部分3D形状的强健特征。 通过仅仅依靠合成数据和自我监督的任务,我们表明,我们的特点不仅比2D基础骨干具有更好的几何理解,而且也是迄今为止部分到部分和部分到完全形状匹配的最佳可用特征。
主要限制可能继承自DINOv3,它涉及对自然图像进行预先训练,从而将偏向形状的倾向纳入直立的方向。
虽然3D对象常被假定为直立的,但这种假设可能会使结果倒向地出场而恶化.
正如补充材料所显示的,虽然我们的方法在倒挂式上仍然超过DINOv3基线,但两种方法的性能都低于其对直立外形的结果。
总体而言,我们的工作表明,通过低级别适应来调整愿景基础模型,可以大大地促进部分理解。
今后,我们的工作还可以扩大到考虑外部杂乱无章和人造物体。
归根结底,我们认为我们的工作是弥合大规模图像表达和三维几何之间差距的一个有希望的步骤,为更广泛的形状分析和三维愿景社区提供了宝贵的见解。

blocks.en:
In this supplementary material, we provide additional details supporting the main paper.
We begin with an overview of the notation (Sec. 7 ) used throughout the method section, followed by extended ablation studies (Sec. 8 ), like runtime comparisons, and a formal definition of the dataset-wide chirality accuracy (Sec. 9 ).
We further describe implementation details (Sec. 10 ), compare our feature representation to those used in prior work (Sec. 11 and 12 ), present failure cases (Sec. 13 ) and analyse the upright bias (Sec. 14 ).
Additionally, we show more real-world scans (Sec. 15 ) and provide additional qualitative results (Sec. 16 ), including feature visualisations.
Finally, we present further 2D/3D application examples (Sec. 17 ) and we give some more insights on rendering with and without texture (Sec. 18 ).

We evaluate different values for hyperparameters, α \alpha and the rank r r in LoRA on the BeCoS validation set in terms of geodesic error (Table 8 ).
The values r = 16 r=16 and α = 32 \alpha=32 yield the best results.
blocks.zh:
我们根据测地误差的BeCoS验证法,对高参数、α-α和LORA的分级r的不同值进行评估(表8)。
数值 r = 16 r = 16 和 α = 32\ alpha = 32 得出最佳结果。

blocks.en: Table 8: LoRA Hyperparameter Ablation: We observe the best results with rank r = 16 r=16 and α = 32 \alpha=32 .
blocks.zh: 表8:LORA超参数 读取 : 我们观测到最佳结果 r = 16 r = 16 和 α = 32\ alpha = 32。

blocks.en:
Table 9 compares the inference time of different methods.
The additional use of stable diffusion in Diff3f results in a longer processing time compared to using DINO features alone.
The other feature descriptors, including our method GeoLoRA, have similar runtimes.
blocks.zh:
表9比较了不同方法的推断时间.
在Diff3f中额外使用稳定的扩散,导致处理时间比仅使用DINO特性要长.
另一个特征描述符,包括我们的方法GeoLORA,也有类似的运行时间.

blocks.en: Table 9: Inference Time Comparison: While DINOv2, DINOv3 and GeoLoRA have similar runtime during inference, Diff3f’s runtime is significantly increased due to the need to additionally run inference with Stable Diffusion.
blocks.zh: 表9:推断时间比较: 虽然DINov2,DINov3和GeoLORA在推论中也有类似的运行时间,但Diff3f的运行时间却因需要额外运行与稳定分泌的推论而大大增加.

blocks.en:
Replacing the ViT-B backbone with a ViT-L backbone does not lead to significant performance gains in terms of geodesic error (see Table 10 ).
Nevertheless, ViT-L requires 50% more training time and twice the amount of VRAM on the GPU than ViT-B.
blocks.zh:
用Vit-L主干取代Vit-B主干不会导致大地测量误差方面的显著性能收益(见表10)。
尽管如此,Vit-L需要的培训时间却比Vit-B多出50%,在GPU上的VRAM数量还要多出两倍.

blocks.en: Table 10 : Performance of Different Backbone Scales: We show that with a larger backbone we do not gain significant improvement in terms of geodesic error.
blocks.zh: 表10: 不同后骨缩放的性能: 我们显示,有了更大的骨干,在大地测量误差方面我们没有取得重大改进。

blocks.en: 10 Additional Implementation Details
blocks.zh: 10 其他执行细节

blocks.en:
For the temperature parameter, we follow [ 3 ] and use τ = 0.07 \tau=0.07 .
We run the training on one A40 GPU and five cores of a Xeon Gold 6248R CPU.
The training takes approximately 5 days for 50,000 50,000 iterations for the longest-lasting BeCoS dataset.
The training time can vary between 2-5 days between the different datasets according to different number of vertices.
As a prompt to Stable Diffusion inside Diff3f, we use ”animal” for animal shapes, ”human” for human shapes and ”centaur” for centaur shapes.
blocks.zh:
对于温度参数,我们遵循[3],并使用\\\tau=0.07=0.07。
我们操作一个A40GPU和一个Xeon Gold 6248RCPU的五个核心的训练.
为期最长的BeCoS数据集的5万次重复培训大约需要5天。
不同的数据集之间根据不同的顶点数量,培训时间可以相差2-5天.
作为Diff3f内部稳定分泌的催化剂,我们对动物形状使用“动物”,对人类形状使用“人类”,对半人马形状使用“摄氏”。

blocks.en: 11 ULRSSM: Comparison to Original Features
blocks.zh: 11 ULRSSM: 与原地物的比较

blocks.en:
Instead of using foundation features or handcrafted descriptors, an alternative approach is to start with the raw XYZ coordinates as input. Since previous methods have shown promising results, for fairness, we also compare our approach with ULRSSM [ 12 ] using XYZ coordinates as input. In Table 11 , we show that the performance falls far behind the use of foundation features.
The use of XYZ is sensitive to shape orientations, which are particularly ambiguous in partial shapes.
blocks.zh:
一种替代办法不是使用地基特征或手工描述符,而是从原始的XYZ坐标开始作为输入. 由于以前的方法已经显示有希望的结果,为了公平起见,我们还将我们的方法与ULRSSM[12]比较,使用XYZ坐标作为输入. 在表11中,我们显示业绩远远落后于使用地基特征。
XYZ的用法对形状取向很敏感,部分形状特别模糊.

blocks.en: Table 11: Comparison of XYZ features vs GeoLoRA features: We compare the geodesic error ( × 100 ) (\times 100) on different partial-to-full datasets with ULRSSM. On all datasets, our features outperform the originally used XYZ features. The numbers in brackets “ ( ) () ” indicate geodesic error results after test-time adaptation [ 12 ] .
blocks.zh: 表11:XYZ特征与GeoLORA特征的比较: 我们比较不同部分到完整数据集的大地测量误差(×100)(\times 100)与ULRSSM. 在所有数据集中,我们的特性都超过了原先使用的XYZ特性. 括号中的数字 " () ( " ) " 表示测试时间调整后测地误差的结果[12]。

blocks.en: 12 Left-Right Prediction: Comparison to Original Features
blocks.zh: 12 左向右预测:与原始特征的比较

blocks.en:
In the main paper, we compare the GeoLoRA features with those of DINOv3.
For completeness, here we report a comparison with the features originally used in [ 58 ] , which combine DINOv2 and Stable Diffusion features (Table 12 ).
blocks.zh:
在主要论文中,我们比较了GeoLORA的地貌特征和DINOv3的地貌特征.
为了完整起见,我们在此报告与[58]中最初使用的特性的比较,这些特性结合了DINov2和稳定分泌特性(表12.).

blocks.en:
Table 12 : Comparison to DINOv2 + Stable Diffusion Features: We compare the chirality (left-right) accuracy of the features used in [ 58 ] to our GeoLoRA features.
Our method’s features show higher accuracy.
blocks.zh:
表12:与DINOv2 + 稳定扩散的比较 特征 : 我们把[58]中使用的特征的奇特性(左 -- -- 右)精度与我们的GeoLORA特征进行比较。
我们的方法的特征显示出更高的准确性。

blocks.en: 13 Failure Cases
blocks.zh: 13起失败案件

blocks.en:
The datasets used to train our models primarily contain upright shapes, resulting in most failure cases involving shapes in different poses, such as a rotated person in a pike position or a person lying on their side with their hands on the ground.
We show two examples in Figure 7 .
blocks.zh:
用于训练我们模型的数据集主要包含直立的形状,导致大多数涉及不同姿势的形状的故障案例,如一个旋转者身处匹克位置,或者一个手放在地上的人倒地上.
我们在图7中举出两个例子。

blocks.en: Figure 7 : Failure Cases: We show two failure cases of our method. The method primarily struggles with shapes in challenging poses, where the shapes are not positioned upright.
blocks.zh: 图7:失败案例: 我们展示了我们方法的两个失败案例。 这种方法主要用有挑战性的姿势来与外形相搏,其中外形没有被平直地定位.

blocks.en: Figure 8 : Additional Results on Real-World Statues from [ 1 ] : DINOv3 fails to find good correspondences between the partial statues and the full template shape, where GeoLoRA finds reasonably dense correspondences.
blocks.zh: 图8:真实世界状况的其他结果,来自[1]: DINOv3未能找到部分雕像与完整模板形状之间的良好对应,GeoLORA在那里发现了相当密集的对应.

blocks.en: 14 Upright Bias
blocks.zh: 14 右派

blocks.en:
For consistency with the literature, we assume that shapes are oriented upright.
However, we train GeoLoRA on FAUST (for 70K iterations), sample random rotation along all axes, and test upside-down partial shapes. GeoLoRA achieves 6.69 geodesic error, while DINOv3 performs 10 × \times worse (63.84).
blocks.zh:
为了与文献保持一致,我们假设形状是直立的。
然而,我们在FAUST上训练GeoLORA(为70K迭代),在所有轴上抽取随机自转,并测试倒向的部分形状. GeoLORA实现6.69个大地测量误差,而DINOv3则执行10×\times worse (63.84).

blocks.en: 15 Additional Real-World Experiments
blocks.zh: 15个额外的真实世界实验

blocks.en:
We demonstrate further real-world scans of statues from [ 1 ] and match them to a template shape from Faust .
Here, GeoLoRA shows qualitatively better matchings than DINOv3.
blocks.zh:
我们从[1]进一步展示真实世界的雕像扫描,并将其与浮士德的模板形状相匹配.
在这里,GeoLORA显示出比DINOv3更好的质量匹配.

blocks.en:
Quantitative evaluation on real-world partial scans is limited by the lack of ground-truth data availability.
Therefore we evaluate the annotated real scan of SHREC20.
Our method significantly reduces geodesic error compared to DINOv3 (5.92 vs. 16.26), indicating improved robustness on real-world data.
blocks.zh:
由于缺乏地面真实数据,对现实世界部分扫描的定量评价受到限制。
因此,我们评价SHREC20的附加说明的真正扫描。
与DINOv3(5.92 vs 16.26)相比,我们的方法大大减少了大地测量误差,表明实际世界数据的稳健性有所提高。

blocks.en: 16 Additional Qualitative Results
blocks.zh: 16 其他定性结果

blocks.en:
We show more qualitative comparisons to other features in Figure 11 .
Additionally, we show further examples of our feature predictions in Figure 12 .
blocks.zh:
我们比较了图11中其他特征的质量。
此外,我们还在图12中展示了我们特征预测的进一步实例。

blocks.en: We show qualitative results for partial-to-partial shape matching in Figure 13 and additional results for partial-to-full shape matching in Figure 14 .
blocks.zh: 图13显示部分到部分形状匹配的质量结果,图14显示部分到全部形状匹配的额外结果。

blocks.en: 17 Further 2D/3D Applications
blocks.zh: 17 此外2D/3D应用程序

blocks.en:
While we focus on learning features for 3D partial shape matching, we find their use in other contexts exciting.
Hence, we use our GeoLoRA model (trained on BeCoS) to perform image matching on SPair-71k [ 42 ] dataset images.
In several cases, our approach provides better matching than DINOv3, especially in images where foreground elements differ in their view (see Table 9 ).
Additionally, we show that our method can also be used for 3D keypoint matching for shapes of the BeCoS test set (see Table 10 ).
blocks.zh:
当我们专注于学习3D部分外形匹配的特征时,我们发现它们在其他场合的使用令人兴奋.
因此,我们使用我们的GeoLORA模型(在BeCoS上训练)在SPair-71k[42]数据集图像上进行图像匹配.
在某些情况下,我们的方法比DINOv3提供更好的匹配,特别是在前景要素观点不同的图像中(见表9)。
此外,我们表明,我们的方法还可以用于BeCoS测试集形状的3D键点匹配(见表10)。

blocks.en: Figure 9 : 2D Keypoint Matching: We show examples for keypoint matching on the SPair-71k [ 42 ] dataset. Our method shows superior matching results in these examples.
blocks.zh: 图9: 2D 关键点匹配: 我们在SPair-71k[42]数据集上显示关键点匹配的例子. 我们的方法显示了这些例子中更好的匹配结果。

blocks.en: Figure 10 : 3D Keypoint Matching: Our method can be used for 3D keypoint matching. We show examples of the BeCoS test set.
blocks.zh: 图10: 三维关键点匹配: 我们的方法可用于3D键点匹配. 我们展示了BeCoS测试集的例子.

blocks.en: 18 Texture & Rendering
blocks.zh: 18 纹理和渲染

blocks.en:
All partial shape matching benchmarks are textureless, so meshes are rendered without texture (single colour with shadow on the surface, see Fig. 2 Image Column).
Using SMPL [ 41 ] , we empirically test texture sensitivity and find that adding texture degrades performance (geodesic error 3.65 vs. 1.32).
We hypothesise that texture helps identify correspondences within the same (e.g., person), but not across different identities (e.g., due to different clothing).
blocks.zh:
所有部分形状匹配的基准都是无纹理的,因此meshes的渲染没有纹理(表面有阴影的单一颜色,参见图2图像列).
使用 SMPL [41],我们经验测试了纹理敏感度,发现添加纹理会降解性能(地极误差3.65对1.32).
我们假设纹理有助于识别同一人(如人)内部的通信,但不会跨越不同的身份(如由不同的衣着所造成).

blocks.en: Figure 11 : Qualitative Results of Feature Quality: We show colour-coded correspondences based on the features computed with different feature extractors. GeoLoRA exhibits improved performance, especially in left-right and front-back predictions.
blocks.zh: 图11:特征质量的定性结果: 我们根据不同特性提取器计算出的特性来显示颜色编码的通信。 GeoLORA展示了更好的性能,特别是在左后方和前后方的预测中.

blocks.en: Figure 12 : More Qualitative Results: We show more qualitative results of our partial-to-full features.
blocks.zh: 图12:质量提高 结果: 我们显示了我们部分到全部特点的更多质量结果。

blocks.en:
Figure 13 : Qualitative Results of Partial-to-Partial Matching: We show colour-coded correspondences for partial-to-partial shape matching methods. We compare DINOv3 features with GeoLoRA features. The red area indicates points that are predicted not to be in the overlapping region.
On the BeCoS dataset and the Psmal dataset, we demonstrate improved performance with GeoLoRA features compared to DINOv3 features.
On CP2P24 we observe similar matching quality.
blocks.zh:
图13:部分对部分的定性结果 匹配情况 : 我们显示颜色编码的对应 部分到部分形状匹配方法。 我们比较了DINOv3的特征与GeoLORA的特征. 红色区域表明,预计不会在重叠区域。
在BeCoS数据集和Psmal数据集上,我们展示了与DINov3特征相比,GeoLORA特征的性能得到改进.
在CP2P24上,我们观察到类似的匹配质量.

blocks.en:
Figure 14 : Qualitative Results of Partial-to-Full Shape Matching Methods: We show two more examples of partial-to-full shape matching on the Pfaust-H and Shrec16 Holes dataset.
We can see improved matching quality with our GeoLoRA features, especially in the extremities of the shapes, such as the left arm of the human and the legs of the horse.
blocks.zh:
图14:部分至全面的质量结果 形状匹配 方法: 我们在Pfaust-H和Shrec16 Holes数据集上又展示了两个部分到完全形状匹配的例子.
我们可以看到与我们的GeoLORA特征的匹配质量得到改善,特别是在外形上,如人和马腿的左臂.
